# `silk/time/codec`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Codecs that read and write the `silk.time` types in any data format of `silk.schema`: as ISO
8601 text with [`TimeText`](#TimeText), or as a Unix time with [`UnixSeconds`](#UnixSeconds) and [`UnixMilliseconds`](#UnixMilliseconds).

## When to use

Use these codecs for a date or time in a field of a type that implements `Schema`. Wrap the
value in a type of your own, and call `Schemas.readVia`, `Schemas.writeVia` and
`Schemas.shapeVia` with the codec from its `read`, `write` and `shape`. Put a codec in a chain
of `silk.schema.codec` to trim the text first or to check the value afterwards.

To read a TOML date or time that is not text, use the TOML codecs of `silk.toml.codec`.

## Details

`TimeText<T>` is implemented for `Instant`, `PlainDate`, `PlainTime`, `PlainDateTime`,
`PlainYearMonth`, `PlainMonthDay`, `Period` and `UtcOffset`. Decoding calls the `parse` of the
type, so it accepts the same text, and fails with `IssueReason.InvalidValue` for other text.
Encoding writes the text that `Display` writes, which `parse` reads back to the same value.

## Gotchas

A Unix time has no fraction below its unit: [`UnixSeconds`](#UnixSeconds) drops the part of an `Instant` below
one second when it encodes, and [`UnixMilliseconds`](#UnixMilliseconds) the part below one millisecond.

## Examples

### Decode a date and write it back

```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.codec { Codec }
import silk.schema.issue { Issue }
import silk.text.string { String }
import silk.time.codec { TimeText }
import silk.time.plain_date { PlainDate }

effect fn nextDay(text: string) -> String ! Issue | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  let codec = TimeText<PlainDate>.make()
  let date = run Codec.decode(&codec, run String.copy(text))
  return run Codec.encode(&codec, &date.addDays(1))
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let written = run Effect.result(nextDay("2026-12-31")) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return match move written {
    Result<String, Issue | OutOfMemoryError>.Success {value} => if value.view() == "2027-01-01" { 0 } else { 1 }
    Result<String, Issue | OutOfMemoryError>.Failure {..} => 2
  }
}
```

Import as `TimeText` with `import silk.time.codec { TimeText }`.

## `TimeText`

```silk
pub struct TimeText<T>
```

The codec between a `silk.time` value `T` and its ISO 8601 text.

### Details

It is implemented for `Instant`, `PlainDate`, `PlainTime`, `PlainDateTime`, `PlainYearMonth`,
`PlainMonthDay`, `Period` and `UtcOffset`. Decoding accepts the text that the `parse` of `T`
accepts, and fails with `IssueReason.InvalidValue` for other text. Encoding writes the text
that `Display` writes for `T`.

<a id="TimeText.kind"></a>

### Field `kind`

```silk
pub kind: [T; 0]
```

Empty. It names the time type.

<a id="UnixSeconds"></a>

## `UnixSeconds`

```silk
pub struct UnixSeconds
```

The codec between an `Instant` and a count of whole seconds from the Unix epoch.

### Details

Decoding fails with `IssueReason.InvalidValue` for a count outside the range of `Instant`.
Encoding rounds down to the second, so an instant before 1970 with a fraction gives the second
before it.

<a id="UnixSeconds.impl.Codec"></a>

## `UnixMilliseconds`

```silk
pub struct UnixMilliseconds
```

The codec between an `Instant` and a count of whole milliseconds from the Unix epoch, the time
value of JavaScript.

### Details

Decoding fails with `IssueReason.InvalidValue` for a count outside the range of `Instant`.
Encoding rounds down to the millisecond.
